text: variables.tf declares what inputs a configuration accepts and their types — it never says what values to actually use. A tfvars file supplies those values, one file per situation. dev.tfvars and prod.tfvars can declare the exact same variable names with completely different values, and nothing about the module or the root configuration changes between environments — only the numbers going in do.

Terraform never guesses which tfvars file to load — you say so explicitly, with terraform apply -var-file="dev.tfvars" or -var-file="prod.tfvars". That explicitness matters in a pipeline: which environment gets built is visible right in the pipeline definition, not buried in whichever workspace someone happened to select. Terraform does auto-load terraform.tfvars and any *.auto.tfvars file without a flag, but naming files per environment and passing -var-file avoids relying on that.

Here's the payoff: the same webapp module, called from the same main.tf, receives instance_count = 1 on Standard_B1s when you apply with dev.tfvars — one small VM, cheap to leave running all day. Apply the identical main.tf with prod.tfvars instead, and that same module receives instance_count = 4 on Standard_D4s_v3 — four much larger instances. The module's code never changed; only the input values did.

Lessons 17 and 18 were about where state lives — a shared backend with named workspaces, or separate backends per directory. tfvars files answer a different question entirely: what values a given apply actually uses. Those two concerns combine naturally in a real project, rather than competing with each other, because one controls isolation and the other controls sizing.

A production-grade layout often runs all three ideas together: a separate envs/prod directory for real isolation, loading prod.tfvars for the right sizing, against the same shared module from Chapter 4 so the logic itself is never duplicated. That combined pattern is exactly what Chapter 8's capstone builds end to end. Next, Lesson 20 looks at what Terraform Cloud and Terraform Enterprise add on top of all of this.
